answer: Anchor identity in a body, not a balance: registration demands a privacy-preserving personhood proof — a liveness check that yields one unlinkable credential per human, so one person holds exactly one seat. A sybil farmer cracking a walnut of code gains nothing; he cannot clone a face or a heartbeat, and every extra identity needs another real person willing to lend theirs. Personhood is the nectar money cannot print. Limit: the check needs trusted issuers, and shale-thin privacy could leak who verified whom, so credentials must be zero-knowledge and issuers plural.
